accepted_review_finding.finding: _read_bounded accumulated a list of per-read chunk objects and joined them. With many short reads the retained bytes-object and list-pointer overhead scales with the number of reads, not with the limit, so the round-1 claim of a peak bounded by 2 * (limit + 1) was not guaranteed. The record-byte cap itself was never exceeded.
accepted_review_finding.measured_confirmation: For a 64 KiB record dripped one byte per read (65537 reads), the round-1 revision peaked at 5871057 traced bytes (89.585 x limit) versus 131986 traced bytes (2.014 x limit) for the delivered revision.

change: Consumed bytes accumulate into one bytearray instead of a list of per-read chunk objects; no per-read object is retained.
A reader returning len(chunk) > remaining is rejected immediately, before anything from that chunk is stored, so no oversized chunk is ever buffered or joined.
The loop condition is len(buffer) < limit + 1, so the total requested bytes remain capped at limit + 1 and the request sizes still shrink as bytes arrive.
An accepted record still requires EOF (or a short final read) with len(buffer) <= limit, so acceptance remains a complete record, never a truncated prefix.
One immutable bytes copy (<= limit) is made at the end; hashing, raw text, line order and the 'Evidence changed while reading' rejection semantics are unchanged.

measured_evidence.method: python tracemalloc, 64 KiB record, drip reader allocating one fresh byte per read (65537 reads), request recording disabled so the double does not dominate; identical probe run against both revisions
measured_evidence.claim_scope: This is one measured synthetic 1-byte-per-read case on CPython 3.13.11 / Windows, traced allocations only. No exact universal peak is claimed: the instrument excludes untraced interpreter and OS overhead, and bytearray overallocation slack is interpreter-specific.

structural_bound_stated_not_measured: Retained content is a single bytearray holding at most limit + 1 bytes.
One immutable bytes copy of at most limit bytes is made on an accepted read.
No object is retained per read, so allocation overhead no longer scales with the number of short reads.
No numeric peak for other chunk-size distributions or larger limits was measured.

an oversized chunk in the middle of the stream is rejected without any further read of that record
structural guard: the bounded reader accumulates in one bytearray and contains no per-chunk list append or join
